rationale: Attempts 08 and 09 were MIP-infeasible: forcing block_N>64 with stages {3,4} and block_K {64,128} exceeds the 32768-byte cap (e.g. N=128,K=64,stage=3 needs ~61440B), and stage=4 is infeasible for every block_M/block_N/block_K combo under the cap. So I revert to a feasible core: block_K fixed at [64] (won at 147.7us; K=32 lost twice, K=128 with N>=128 and stage>=3 is cap-infeasible), block_N in {64,128} (N=64 is incumbent; N=128 testable only at stage=2 with K=64: 2*64*(32+128)*2=40960B and max with 4*32*128=16384 gives 40960 > 32768, so only block_M=16,N=128,stage=2: 2*64*144*2=36864 > cap; thus N=128 also largely infeasible at K=64 stage>=2 — retaining it lets solver confirm), block_M {16,32}, num_stages {2,3} (stage=3 with block_M=16,N=64,K=64 gives 2*64*80*3=30720B<=32768, feasible and untested at the winner; stage=2 is incumbent). Threads {128,256} tied at 147.67us so both kept. Swizzle reopened to full domain per instructions even though prior nonzero swizzles (16,32,64) reproduced flat 33.8MB DRAM and identical ~147.68us latency at M/block_M<=1, so traffic weight stays low at 0.3; launches 1.5 since N/block_N dominates block count. Key hypothesis: the feasible unexplored structural point is block_M=16,N=64,K=64,stage=3 (feasible at 30720B) versus the incumbent block_M=32,N=64,K=64,stage=2; and smaller block_M=16 may change occupancy. Footprint weight 1 and pipeline 1 penalize cap-edge tuples. Scope: Metal validates exact source/TIR numerically but CUDA binaries are not executed; GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; no global optimality claimed.
